description: Hot and Sour Soup is a classic Chinese appetizer, renowned for its intriguing balance of piquant spice and tangy vinegar. This warming and savory broth, typically loaded with shredded pork, tofu, and mushrooms, offers a delightful texture and an unforgettable flavor experience. It is a comforting and invigorating dish perfect for any occasion.

instructions.title: Prepare Ingredients
instructions.text: Rehydrate dried shiitake and wood ear mushrooms in hot water for 20-30 minutes. Drain, squeeze dry, and thinly slice or shred. Shred pork loin, firm tofu, and bamboo shoots. Beat eggs in a small bowl. Prepare cornstarch slurry by mixing cornstarch with cold water.

instructions.title: Sauté Pork
instructions.text: Heat a tablespoon of cooking oil in a large pot or wok over medium-high heat. Add shredded pork and stir-fry until it changes color and is lightly browned, about 3-4 minutes. Remove pork from the pot and set aside.

instructions.title: Build the Broth
instructions.text: Pour chicken broth into the same pot. Add the rehydrated mushrooms, shredded bamboo shoots, and shredded tofu. Bring the broth to a rolling boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer and let it cook for 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld together.

instructions.title: Season the Soup
instructions.text: Return the cooked pork to the pot. Stir in the soy sauce, rice vinegar, and white pepper. Taste the soup and adjust the seasonings as needed, adding more vinegar or pepper to achieve your desired balance of hot and sour flavor.

instructions.title: Thicken and Add Eggs
instructions.text: Slowly drizzle the cornstarch slurry into the simmering soup while stirring constantly until the soup reaches your desired thickness. Gradually pour in the beaten eggs in a thin, continuous stream, stirring gently to create delicate egg ribbons throughout the soup. Remove the pot from the heat.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Ladle the hot and sour soup into individual serving bowls. Drizzle with a few drops of sesame oil and chili oil for an extra layer of flavor and heat. Garnish generously with fresh chopped green onions before serving immediately.

tips: For maximum flavor, use a high-quality chicken broth or even homemade stock. If using store-bought, opt for a low-sodium variety to better control the overall saltiness.
Adjust the amount of white pepper and rice vinegar to your personal preference for heat and sourness. It is always easier to add more later than to remove it.
When thickening the soup with cornstarch slurry, ensure it is well-mixed and add it slowly while stirring vigorously to prevent lumps and achieve a smooth consistency.
article:
Unleash your taste buds into a world of invigorating flavors with a bowl of Hot and Sour Soup. This iconic Chinese appetizer is celebrated globally for its unique blend of tangy vinegar, fiery white pepper, and savory umami notes, all brought together in a comforting, thick broth. More than just a starter, Hot and Sour Soup is a culinary experience that awakens the senses, offering warmth, spice, and a delightful complexity that leaves a lasting impression. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a kitchen novice, mastering this classic dish at home is a rewarding journey that promises delicious results.

## What is Hot and Sour Soup?
At its heart, Hot and Sour Soup is a traditional Szechuan-style soup characterized by its signature "hot" (spicy) and "sour" (tangy) profile. The heat typically comes from a generous dose of white pepper, sometimes augmented with chili oil, while the sourness is primarily derived from rice vinegar. Beyond these defining flavors, the soup boasts a rich, savory depth from ingredients like soy sauce, sesame oil, and often a flavorful broth base.

Visually, Hot and Sour Soup is a feast for the eyes, with its dark, glossy broth brimming with an array of finely shredded or diced ingredients. Common components include slivers of pork, soft cubes of tofu, earthy dried shiitake and wood ear mushrooms, crunchy bamboo shoots, and delicate ribbons of cooked egg. The broth itself is typically thickened with a cornstarch slurry, giving it a velvety texture that coats the palate beautifully. It’s a dish that embodies the harmonious balance fundamental to Chinese cuisine, where contrasting flavors and textures come together to create a profoundly satisfying whole.

## Ingredients You'll Need
Crafting an authentic Hot and Sour Soup requires a thoughtful selection of ingredients. Here’s what you’ll need to gather:

For the Broth Base:
* 6 cups chicken or vegetable broth
* 2 cups water (if using concentrated broth)

For Flavor and Seasoning:
* 1/4 cup rice vinegar (or more to taste)
* 3 tablespoons light soy sauce
* 1 tablespoon dark soy sauce (for color and deeper flavor)
* 1 teaspoon sesame oil
* 1-2 teaspoons ground white pepper (adjust to desired heat)
* 1/2 teaspoon sugar (to balance flavors)
* Optional: 1-2 teaspoons chili oil for extra heat

For Solids and Textures:
* 4-5 dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated and thinly sliced
* 1/2 oz dried wood ear mushrooms, rehydrated and thinly sliced
* 4 oz pork loin or tenderloin, thinly shredded (or substitute with chicken or omit for vegetarian)
* 8 oz firm or silken tofu, drained and cut into 1/2-inch cubes
* 1 (8 oz) can bamboo shoots, drained and julienned
* 2 large eggs, beaten

For Thickening:
* 3 tablespoons cornstarch
* 1/4 cup cold water

For Garnish:
* 2 scallions, thinly sliced
* Fresh cilantro, chopped (optional)

## Step-by-Step Instructions
Making Hot and Sour Soup at home is simpler than you might think. Follow these steps for a delicious result:

1.  **Prepare Dried Ingredients:** Place dried shiitake and wood ear mushrooms in separate bowls. Cover with hot water and let them soak for at least 20-30 minutes until softened. Once soft, drain, squeeze out excess water, remove stems from shiitake, and thinly slice both types of mushrooms.
2.  **Prepare Other Solids:** While mushrooms rehydrate, thinly shred the pork. Cut the tofu into small cubes and julienne the bamboo shoots. Beat the eggs in a small bowl and set aside.
3.  **Combine Broth and Seasonings:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, combine the chicken or vegetable broth and water (if using). Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Add the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, white pepper, and sugar. Stir well to combine.
4.  **Add Meats and Vegetables:** Add the shredded pork, rehydrated mushrooms, and bamboo shoots to the simmering broth. Cook for 5-7 minutes, or until the pork is cooked through.
5.  **Add Tofu:** Gently stir in the cubed tofu. Be careful not to break up the delicate pieces.
6.  **Thicken the Soup:** In a small bowl, whisk together the cornstarch and cold water to create a smooth slurry. Slowly pour the cornstarch slurry into the simmering soup in a steady stream, stirring continuously. Continue to stir until the soup thickens to your desired consistency. This usually takes 1-2 minutes.
7.  **Create Egg Ribbons:** With the soup at a gentle simmer, slowly pour the beaten eggs into the soup in a thin stream while stirring clockwise with a spoon or ladle. The eggs will cook instantly, forming delicate ribbons.
8.  **Final Adjustments and Garnish:** Taste the Hot and Sour Soup and adjust seasonings as needed. You might want more vinegar for tang, more white pepper for heat, or a pinch more salt. Stir in chili oil if desired. Ladle into bowls and garnish with sliced scallions and fresh cilantro before serving.

## Pro Tips for the Best Hot and Sour Soup
Achieving that perfect balance of "hot" and "sour" is key to an outstanding Hot and Sour Soup.

*   **Balance is Everything:** The beauty of this soup lies in its equilibrium. Start with the recommended amounts of vinegar and white pepper, then taste and adjust. Add vinegar a teaspoon at a time for sourness and white pepper for heat. Remember, you can always add more, but you can't take it away!
*   **Quality Ingredients:** Using high-quality broth, fresh mushrooms, and good rice vinegar will elevate the flavor significantly. Don't skimp on the white pepper; it's crucial for the authentic "hot" element.
*   **Cornstarch Slurry Technique:** Ensure your cornstarch slurry is lump-free before adding it. Pour it slowly into the simmering soup while stirring constantly to prevent clumping and achieve an even thickness. If the soup is too thick, you can add a little more broth or water. If it's not thick enough, mix a bit more cornstarch with cold water and add it incrementally.
*   **Egg Ribbons:** For delicate egg ribbons, ensure your soup is at a gentle simmer, not a rolling boil. Pour the beaten egg slowly through a fork or a fine-mesh sieve while stirring the soup in one direction.
*   **Don't Overcook:** Once the pork is cooked and the soup is thickened, avoid prolonged boiling, as it can break down the ingredients and diminish the freshness of the flavors.

## Serving Suggestions
Hot and Sour Soup is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in various ways.

*   **As an Appetizer:** This is its most common role in Chinese restaurants. A small bowl before a main course is the perfect palate cleanser and stimulant.
*   **Light Meal:** Paired with a side of steamed rice or a simple green salad, a larger bowl of Hot and Sour Soup can make a satisfying and comforting light meal on its own, especially on a chilly day.
*   **Part of a Feast:** Serve it alongside other Chinese favorites like fried rice, stir-fried noodles, spring rolls, or General Tso's chicken for a complete and authentic dining experience.
*   **Garnish Generously:** Always finish with a sprinkle of fresh scallions. A drizzle of extra chili oil for those who like it spicier, or a dash of black vinegar for an extra layer of sourness, can enhance the experience.

## Variations and Substitutions
The beauty of Hot and Sour Soup lies in its adaptability. Don't hesitate to customize it to your preferences or dietary needs.

*   **Vegetarian/Vegan:** Easily make this soup vegetarian by using vegetable broth and omitting the pork. Increase the amount of tofu or add other vegetables like sliced carrots, baby corn, or water chestnuts. For a vegan version, ensure you use a plant-based broth and omit the egg, possibly replacing it with extra silken tofu for creaminess.
*   **Different Proteins:** Instead of pork, you can use shredded chicken breast, thinly sliced beef, or even shrimp. Add shrimp towards the very end, as they cook quickly.
*   **Mushroom Medley:** Experiment with different types of dried or fresh mushrooms, such as oyster mushrooms or enoki mushrooms, for varied textures and flavors.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the white pepper to your liking. For a milder soup, use less; for more heat, add an extra teaspoon or two, or incorporate fresh finely minced red chilies or a bit of Szechuan chili bean paste.
*   **Extra Tang:** If you crave more sourness, add an extra splash of rice vinegar just before serving. A few drops of Chinkiang black vinegar can also add a deeper, more complex sour note.
*   **Gluten-Free:** Substitute regular soy sauce with tamari to make the soup gluten-free. Ensure your broth is also gluten-free.

Hot and Sour Soup is more than just a dish; it's a testament to the dynamic and diverse flavors of Chinese cuisine. Its unique combination of heat, tang, and umami makes it a truly unforgettable culinary experience. By following this guide, you can easily bring the authentic taste of this beloved classic into your own kitchen, creating a comforting and invigorating bowl of warmth that will impress family and friends alike. Enjoy the journey of crafting your perfect bowl of Hot and Sour Soup!
